F01.goal: Create a usable wallet for receiving and spending or monitoring funds.
F01.reason: Standard, encrypted, watch-only and external-signer creation achieve the main wallet-creation goal. Standalone blank-wallet creation remains a secondary gap.

F02.goal: Open, select and close the wallets the user wants to work with.
F02.reason: Opening, keeping several wallets loaded, switching and closing each wallet achieve the goal. Closing all wallets requires repeated individual actions.

F03.goal: Protect a wallet with a backup and recover it when needed.
F03.reason: Backup and supported-file restoration work, and filename-based naming is equivalent. Recovery of legacy backups still lacks a supported restore-and-migrate flow.

F04.goal: Convert an existing legacy wallet into a usable current-format wallet.
F04.reason: Migration, backup preservation and access to the migrated wallet are implemented. Automatic opening changes the sequence, not the migration outcome.

F05.goal: Export a portable wallet copy that monitors funds without spending keys.
F05.reason: Creating a new watch-only wallet does not provide an export of the existing spending wallet. The watch-only wallet-file export outcome is absent.

F06.goal: Protect spending keys and authorize temporary access with a passphrase.
F06.reason: Encryption, passphrase changes, temporary unlocking and automatic relocking achieve key protection. Missing live lock-status display remains a separate visibility gap.

F07.goal: Understand which wallet funds are available, pending, or immature, and review recent activity.
F07.reason: Wallet funds, pending payments, recent activity and synchronization status are visible. Pending payments are verified, but the displayed balance can stay stale when mining rewards mature. That observed incorrect balance keeps the overview partial.

F08.goal: Generate and share a receiving destination or reusable payment request.
F08.reason: Address generation, request details, QR codes and request reuse achieve the receiving goal. File/clipboard sharing replaces dragging; device address verification remains a specific unsupported capability.

F09.goal: Prepare and send the intended payment with reliable recipient information.
F09.reason: Payment preparation, signing, broadcast and recipient notes work. Selected-recipient fee deduction remains unsupported, so this group stays partial. The note-preservation test failure was resolved by fixing the script input.

F10.goal: Turn a Bitcoin payment request into a prepared payment.
F10.reason: Entering, pasting, importing or dropping a request populates the payment details. Automatic operating-system forwarding is a different entry path, not required for the main request-to-payment outcome.

F11.goal: Choose a fee appropriate to the desired confirmation speed.
F11.reason: Estimated targets, custom rates, fee review and unavailable-estimate feedback provide the intended fee choice.

F12.goal: Choose and control which coins fund a payment.
F12.reason: Input selection, grouping, locking and selected-funds review achieve funding control. Clipboard details, explicit confirmation counts and custom change destinations remain secondary limitations.

F13.goal: Prepare and transfer an unsigned transaction for later signing.
F13.reason: PSBT file export provides the signing handoff without clipboard support. Wallets holding only some required multisig keys still cannot use the unsigned-payment flow, leaving a real wallet-compatibility gap.

F14.goal: Review, advance signing and broadcast an imported PSBT.
F14.reason: File import/export supplies the transfer paths, but partial local multisig signing and some recipient/output-script cases are unsupported. These block transaction workflows rather than just alternative controls.

F15.goal: Use an external device to keep keys separate and authorize wallet activity.
F15.reason: External signing and key separation are connected, but users cannot verify receiving addresses on the device. That trusted-device check is a substantive missing capability.

F16.goal: Find, inspect and export wallet transaction activity.
F16.reason: History search, filters, details and CSV export achieve the review and record-keeping goal. Fixed sorting and limited clipboard/label editing remain secondary differences.

F17.goal: Resolve unconfirmed transactions and recover spending flexibility.
F17.reason: Fee increases work, but abandonment and fee-bump PSBT export are absent. Users cannot complete those recovery or external-signing paths.

F18.goal: Maintain and reuse labeled payment-address records.
F18.reason: Receiving addresses can be viewed, labeled and copied. Sending-contact management and address-record export are absent, leaving a substantial part of address-book use unavailable.

F19.goal: Sign a message or check that a signature proves control of an address.
F19.reason: Message signing, verification, encrypted-wallet access and signature copying achieve the goal for the supported address type.

F20.goal: Set up storage and synchronize a usable node.
F20.reason: Data-directory selection, pruning, storage checks, network selection and synchronization feedback achieve setup. Missing wallet-recovery guidance does not block the main setup workflow.

F21.goal: Configure node connectivity and manage peer access.
F21.reason: Network routing/settings, peer inspection, disconnection and bans provide connectivity control. Copying entries from the ban list remains a secondary convenience gap.

F22.goal: Inspect node behavior and perform advanced operations.
F22.reason: Node/traffic/log views and wallet-aware RPC tools provide diagnostics and command access. Selectable time ranges provide focused observation without clearing traffic history.

F23.goal: Adjust and recover application behavior through supported preferences.
F23.reason: Many settings and startup reset are available, and an external editor is an equivalent configuration path. Missing spending-policy preferences and startup integration still prevent some requested behavior choices. The new functional check also found that the database-cache editor rejects normal allocations above 8 MiB.

F24.goal: Keep the node accessible in the background and restore or quit it.
F24.reason: Tray/Dock visibility, background operation and quit behavior achieve the shell goal. Restoring the main window before using task menus replaces duplicate tray shortcuts.

F25.goal: Receive transaction and application notifications through the desktop.
F25.reason: Desktop notification delivery is not connected. Critical in-app dialogs cover a fallback subfeature, but do not implement the main desktop-notification channel.

F26.goal: Manage application visibility, placement and access to wallet and node views.
F26.reason: Window placement/visibility persist, background operation works, and wallet/node views remain accessible. Switching views replaces a separate diagnostics window.

F27.goal: Start and stop the node predictably, including recovery and system shutdown.
F27.reason: Normal startup, cancellation and clean exit work. Unreadable-settings recovery and Windows session-shutdown coordination have no equivalent supported flow.

F28.goal: Reach common wallet and node tasks and switch active wallets.
F28.reason: Application navigation, wallet selection, menus and shortcuts provide the intended task access.

F29.goal: Understand the current state of the node and active wallet.
F29.reason: Connectivity, sync and amount units are visible, but live wallet lock and key-generation state are missing. These are unavailable state information, not layout differences.

F30.goal: Understand application feedback and make informed operation decisions.
F30.reason: Messages, confirmations, busy states and sync progress/ETA achieve the main feedback goal. General wallet/rescan progress remains a specific gap; a separate sync-rate number is not required.

F31.goal: Integrate wallet use with desktop behavior and application help.
F31.reason: Explicit request import and manual theme choice achieve their user outcomes. Missing macOS background-throttling protection and command-line help access remain substantive gaps.

F32.goal: Conceal wallet values and activity with a persistent privacy preference.
F32.reason: There is no equivalent balance/activity masking or history-restriction workflow.

F33.goal: Run and manage a node without enabling wallet features.
F33.reason: Wallet-disabled operation retains node tools, preferences and the application shell.

F34.goal: Rediscover wallet history while monitoring and controlling a rescan.
F34.reason: RPC can initiate rescanning as the baseline allows, but the GUI lacks rescan progress and cancellation. The monitored, controllable rescan outcome is incomplete.
